dialogue_turns.text:
The latest email is from Suno, dated 10 August 2026, titled “Terms of service changes to your Pro subscription.”

Bottom line: no confirmation click is required. If you continue using Suno after 3 September 2026, you will automatically accept the new terms.

Changes:

- Pro downloads will be limited to 20 songs per billing month. The limit applies to existing songs too; listening and sharing remain unlimited. Downloads reset on your billing date and unused downloads do not roll over. [Suno FAQ](https://help.suno.com/en/articles/13614785)
- Suno says music downloaded while you are a paid subscriber retains commercial and personal-use rights. Commercial use is tied to having a permitted paid-plan download. [Suno announcement](https://suno.com/blog/suno-updates-tos) · [new Terms](https://suno.com/terms-september-2026)
- Disputes will be subject to updated individual arbitration provisions, including class-action and jury-trial waivers. [New Terms](https://suno.com/terms-september-2026)

What you should do:

- If you are happy to continue: no mandatory action. Consider downloading important songs and stems before 3 September, especially if you have more than 20 tracks to save.
- For commercial releases: ensure each track has been downloaded through your paid Pro plan.
- If you reject the terms: stop using Suno and close the account before your renewal date or within 30 days of 3 September, whichever comes first.

Separate billing note: I also found a failed-payment notice from 6 August, but a receipt dated 8 August confirms a successful US$10 Pro payment, so there does not appear to be an immediate billing issue.
